Mongolram.description: A laborer with no fixed abode, who becomes a murder victim early in the narrative.

Gunomoy Das.description: A middle-aged, unhappy shopkeeper with a quarrelsome wife, who is murdered with a porcupine quill.

Gunomoy Babu.description: Another reference to Gunomoy Das, highlighting his social status.

Rakhalbabu.description: A police inspector involved in the investigation of the murders, who consults Byomkesh.

Byomkesh.description: The central detective figure, known as a 'truth-seeker', who investigates the murders.

Ajit.description: Byomkesh's close friend and chronicler, present during the investigation.

Debashis.description: A young man who owns a house in South Calcutta, later married to Deepa.

Deepa.description: Debashis's wife, a young woman from an aristocratic, orthodox family, struggling with her marriage.

Nakulesh.description: The long-serving servant and cook in Debashis's household.

Nripati Laha.description: A well-educated, wealthy bachelor who hosts social gatherings (adda) and acts as a matchmaker.

Neelamadhab.description: Deepa's father, a college professor and a man of strong will.

Udayamadhab Mukherjee.description: Deepa's authoritative grandfather, a retired college principal who rules the family.

Bijoyamadhab.description: Deepa's elder brother, an M.A. in Sanskrit, actively involved in arranging her marriage.

Probal.description: A sensitive musician and singer, formerly a friend of Debashis, now living in reduced circumstances.

Kapil Bose.description: A wealthy, well-educated young man, friend of Nripati, known for his discerning nature.

Kharga Bahadur.description: A renowned Nepali-Bengali football player, humble despite his fame.

Sujan Mitra.description: A rising film star, known for his versatility and modesty, part of the adda group.

Shubhashis Babu.description: Debashis's deceased father, former owner of Prajapati Cosmetics.

Deepankari.description: A name used by Udayamadhab for Deepa, reflecting affection and tradition.

Garia.description: A neighborhood in South Calcutta where Gunomoy Babu's home is located.

Rabindra Sarobar.description: A prominent lake and park area in South Calcutta, known for its scenic beauty.

Calcutta.description: The former name of Kolkata, a major city in eastern India and the setting for much of the story.

Keyatala.description: A locality in South Calcutta where Byomkesh resides.

South Calcutta Improvement Trust.description: A civic body responsible for urban development in South Calcutta.

Chaitra.description: A month in the Bengali calendar, corresponding to March-April.

Poush.description: A winter month in the Bengali calendar, roughly December-January.

Senior Cambridge.description: A British school-leaving examination, indicating Deepa's level of education.

Ballygunge.description: A well-known, upscale neighborhood in South Calcutta.

Delhi University.description: A prestigious university in India's capital, where Debashis studied.

Prajapati Cosmetics.description: A fictional cosmetics factory founded by Debashis's father.

Barujje.description: A colloquial Bengali term for 'Bandyopadhyay', a Brahmin surname.

Shandilya gotra.description: A Brahmin lineage or clan, significant in Hindu caste identity.

Kestonagar.description: A locality known for its clay idol makers, referenced to describe Sujan's features.

Utapala Cinema.description: A cinema hall in Calcutta, mentioned as a local entertainment venue.

Gita.description: A sacred Hindu scripture, referenced in a conversation about caste.

Lord Krishna.description: A major Hindu deity, quoted in context of the Gita and caste discussion.

Barendra.description: A Brahmin sub-group, referenced in the context of marriage customs.

Chatterjee, Banerjee, Ganguly, Ghoshal.description: Common Bengali Brahmin surnames, indicating caste and family lineage.

Kathmandu.description: The capital of Nepal, mentioned as the site of Kharga Bahadur's postponed wedding.

Nepal.description: A neighboring country to India, home to Kharga Bahadur's family.

babu.description: A respectful term for a gentleman, often used after a name.

panjabi.description: A traditional knee-length tunic worn by Bengali men.

baithak-khana.description: A drawing room or formal sitting room in a Bengali household.

adda.description: An informal gathering for conversation, often among friends.

boudi.description: A term for elder brother's wife; sister-in-law.

dada-babu.description: A respectful way to address the master of the house, combining 'elder brother' and 'sir'.

luchi.description: A deep-fried, puffed Bengali bread made from refined flour.

alur dom.description: A Bengali dish of spiced potatoes, often served with luchi.

sandesh.description: A Bengali sweet made from fresh paneer or chhena.

dhoti.description: A traditional Indian garment, a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

anchal.description: The loose end of a sari, often draped over the shoulder.

bou-bhaat.description: A post-wedding ritual in Bengali culture, where the bride is formally welcomed into the groom's house.

takht.description: A low wooden platform or cot, often used for seating in traditional Bengali homes.

harmonium.description: A hand-pumped keyboard instrument commonly used in Indian music.

kukri.description: A traditional curved knife from Nepal, often used as a gift or symbol.

gotra.description: A Hindu lineage or clan, important in marriage arrangements.

palti.description: A term denoting a particular family or lineage, significant in Bengali caste and marriage customs.

varna.description: The Hindu concept of social order or caste.

ashrama.description: A stage of life in Hindu philosophy, or sometimes a hermitage.

purdah.description: A practice of female seclusion prevalent in some Indian communities.
